lookup.sheSays: "I can't say to VMware we've tested another option."
lookup.weDo: build a tested way back before anything moves
lookup.supportingFact: Nutanix Move can create test VMs on the target site in an isolated network, and built-in rollback options keep the source VM (disconnected and annotated). Vendor blog.
lookup.caution: Say what we BUILD together. Don't say Nutanix removes all risk.
lookup.causeQuestion: To what extent is having no tested alternative weakening your position with VMware?
lookup.impactQuestion: Is the board asking what your plan B is, and is that a concern right now?

lookup.sheSays: "If it goes wrong mid-migration, patient systems go down."
lookup.weDo: start with non-critical workloads, test first, and agree the cutover windows with your clinical teams
lookup.supportingFact: Move pre-seeds data and does delta syncs so cutovers cause minimal disruption. The page gives no downtime figures.
lookup.caution: NEVER promise zero downtime. 'I can't promise zero downtime, what would you need in a plan?'
lookup.causeQuestion: To what extent is the risk of an outage during a move what is holding you back?
lookup.impactQuestion: If a migration went wrong, who would feel it first, and how?

lookup.sheSays: "The CFO has to defend a number to the board."
lookup.weDo: cost it side by side with your VMware quote, using your actual numbers
lookup.supportingFact: Nutanix says the AHV hypervisor is included in its licences at no additional cost, and existing vSphere licences can be applied to the platform. Vendor claim.
lookup.caution: Do NOT say it will be cheaper. Say: 'I haven't seen your estate, that's what the comparison is for.'
lookup.causeQuestion: To what extent is a lack of real numbers on the alternatives a problem when you talk to finance?
lookup.impactQuestion: How is finance reacting to the jump, and is that a concern right now?

lookup.sheSays: "The quote is more than double what we pay now."
lookup.weDo: put a costed comparison next to your renewal quote before the board meets
lookup.supportingFact: Same licensing points as above (AHV included, vSphere licence mobility). Vendor claim.
lookup.caution: Never promise a saving. Compare, don't claim.
lookup.causeQuestion: To what extent is the licensing change driving the increase, compared with what you actually use?
lookup.impactQuestion: What gets cut or delayed if the quote stands, and is that a concern right now?

lookup.sheSays: "My team is stretched and only knows VMware."
lookup.weDo: put our engineer and the reseller alongside your team, with training time agreed up front
lookup.supportingFact: Nutanix lists migration tools, training, professional services and a migration blueprint. Vendor claim.
lookup.caution: Ask: 'Training time, or support during the move?' Don't promise a learning-curve length.
lookup.causeQuestion: To what extent is your team's time, or only knowing one platform, an issue?
lookup.impactQuestion: What does it cost the hospital when the team is tied up with this?

lookup.sheSays: "The arrays go out of support at the end of next year."
lookup.weDo: keep the storage replacement in the same plan, so it's sorted before the arrays go out of support
lookup.supportingFact: Nutanix positions hyperconverged infrastructure as a SAN replacement, and says it can also run alongside an existing SAN for current workloads. Vendor claim.
lookup.caution: The date comes from HER. Don't say it fixes the storage on its own, say it goes in the plan.
lookup.causeQuestion: To what extent is the end-of-support date on the arrays forcing the timing?
lookup.impactQuestion: What happens to patient-facing systems if the arrays fail before they're replaced?

lookup.painType: Servers and storage as two worlds
lookup.sheSays: "Vendors blame each other and my people are stuck in the middle."
lookup.weDo: bring servers, storage and networking into one system you manage from one place
lookup.supportingFact: A healthcare customer (Gruppo Policlinico di Monza, 2020) said production and DR are managed centrally through Prism. Vendor press release, single customer.
lookup.caution: One customer, 2020, vendor-published. Use as 'one hospital group did X', never as a general promise.
lookup.causeQuestion: To what extent does managing servers and storage separately slow you down when something breaks?
lookup.impactQuestion: How much team time goes on vendors pointing at each other, and is that a concern right now?

lookup.sheSays: "Patient systems are the one thing I can't be wrong about."
lookup.weDo: agree migration windows with your clinical teams and name an engineer who is on call during the cutover
lookup.supportingFact: The same customer reported RPO and RTO down 80% on average and storage snapshots at minute intervals. Vendor claim, one customer.
lookup.caution: Don't quote the 80% as a promise. Only if she asks for evidence, and name the source.
lookup.causeQuestion: To what extent does clinical uptime limit how and when you can change anything?
lookup.impactQuestion: Who in the clinical teams feels it first when systems are unstable?

lookup.sheSays: "The board wants us less dependent on one vendor."
lookup.weDo: give you a tested alternative on the table before the board meets, so you're not tied to one quote
lookup.supportingFact: Nutanix Move migrates VMware workloads to AHV on-premises, to edge, and to public cloud. Vendor blog.
lookup.caution: Never run down VMware. She chose it and it has worked for ten years.
lookup.causeQuestion: To what extent is the board's push on single-vendor risk shaping the decision?
lookup.impactQuestion: How would it look at the board if you signed the renewal with no alternative?

lookup.sheSays: "Anything touching patient systems needs the compliance lead's sign-off."
lookup.weDo: bring in a compliance expert to answer in writing, and agree who covers it on your side
lookup.supportingFact: The Monza release names GDPR requirements and security as goals but states no specific security outcome.
lookup.caution: Don't claim compliance. 'I'd want an expert to answer that. Who covers it on your side?'
lookup.causeQuestion: To what extent does compliance sign-off slow or shape any change to patient systems?
lookup.impactQuestion: Who covers compliance on your side, and what would they need to see?

lookup.painType: Paying for a suite we don't use
lookup.sheSays: "We're paying for a lot we don't use."
lookup.weDo: map what you actually use against what you're being quoted for
lookup.supportingFact: No public Nutanix source. This is a discovery step you run with her.
lookup.sourceStatus: Role-play / your own plan, not a Nutanix claim
lookup.caution: Don't claim savings. It's a question, not a promise.
lookup.causeQuestion: To what extent are you paying for parts of the licence you don't use?
lookup.impactQuestion: What would that money otherwise go to?

lookup.weDo: cost a replacement side by side with extending the old hardware's warranty, using your real numbers, before the budget window closes
lookup.caution: Don't promise it is cheaper or that it prevents outages.
lookup.causeQuestion: To what extent is ageing hardware behind the outages you've had?
lookup.impactQuestion: When that system goes down, who feels it first, and what do they do?

basics.say_plainly: It puts your servers, your storage and your networking into one system, so you manage it all from one place instead of three separate things.
Servers, storage and networking handled in software on standard hardware, managed in one place.
The hypervisor that runs the virtual machines. Nutanix says it is included in the licence at no additional cost.
The management console. One hospital group said it manages production and disaster recovery centrally through it, including upgrades and troubleshooting.
basics.source: Nutanix press release, 2020 (vendor claim, one customer): https://www.nutanix.com/press-releases/2020/gruppo-policlinico-di-monza-healthcare-system-chooses-nutanix-to-improve-security-reliability-and-dr

basics.she_asks: How would we move our VMs?
basics.say_plainly: A tool called Nutanix Move. It copies the data across ahead of time, can test the VMs in an isolated network first, and has rollback options that keep the original VM. It doesn't give a downtime figure, so never promise zero.

basics.she_asks: Do we have to throw out our current storage?
basics.say_plainly: Nutanix says it can run alongside an existing SAN, or replace it. Which fits depends on your estate, so that's part of the comparison.

basics.she_asks: Can we use our existing VMware licences?
basics.say_plainly: Nutanix says existing vSphere licences can be applied to its platform. I'd want to check your exact licences in the comparison.

basics.she_asks: Why are customers looking at Nutanix?
basics.say_plainly: Broadcom bought VMware, not merged, causing price hikes and licensing changes that are pushing customers to look elsewhere, including Nutanix.
About $2.55B annual recurring revenue (ARR), up 16%, with 3,000+ new customers, and the CEO expects lots of VMware migration over the next five years. Only if she asks; don't push it.

objections.say_this: "That's the right thing to worry about. I can't promise zero downtime, and nobody honest can. What would you need to see in a plan to feel safe?"
objections.why_it_works: Admitting the limit earns trust. Her answer is the safety plan.
objections.never_say: zero downtime, or any specific downtime figure

objections.say_this: "That's a real cost, so we put it in the comparison. What would help most: training time, or someone supporting you during the move?"
objections.why_it_works: You treat the cost as real and give her a choice.
objections.never_say: any specific learning-curve length (e.g. 'in three weeks')

objections.she_says: "Is it cheaper? The reseller said so."
objections.say_this: "I can't promise that, because I haven't seen your setup yet. What would you need to see to know if it's worth it?"  Then: "You said [her ceiling] is what you can absorb. Is that still true?"
objections.why_it_works: You refuse to promise what you can't prove. It leads to the costed comparison.

objections.she_says: "What about compliance? This is patient data."
objections.say_this: "That's a big one, and I'd want an expert to answer it properly, not me. Who looks after that on your side?"
objections.why_it_works: Honest, and you get the compliance lead's name for the buying box.
objections.never_say: claim compliance yourself — that requires an expert

objections.she_says: "Can you prove it will work for us?"
objections.say_this: "I can't prove that today. That's exactly what the comparison is for."
objections.why_it_works: Turns 'no' into the reason for the next meeting.
objections.never_say: I can prove it will work for you

objections.she_says: what about the warranty gap / we'd lose our warranty
objections.shes_worried: She's worried she'll have no vendor support if hardware fails during a migration
objections.say_this: That's a fair concern. I can't promise a warranty transfer — what would you need to see in a plan to feel covered? We can map what the gap looks like before anything moves.
objections.why_it_works: Agree, admit the limit, ask what she needs, bridge to the plan. No claim about Nutanix.
objections.never_say: Nutanix covers the warranty / you won't have a gap

slips_to_avoid: ARR means annual recurring revenue, not 'average'
Never put words in her mouth
